short: The Big Three Allied leaders met in Iran to coordinate military strategy, confirming plans for the invasion of France.
full:
Between 28 November and 1 December 1943, US President Franklin D. Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin met for the first time at the Tehran Conference in Iran. The central achievement of the meeting was the Western Allies' commitment to open a second front in Europe by launching Operation Overlord, the invasion of northern France, by May 1944. In return, Stalin pledged to launch a simultaneous major offensive on the Eastern Front.

The conference also addressed the post-war political landscape, including preliminary discussions about the United Nations and the shifting of Poland's borders westward. The successful coordination at Tehran represented the high point of Allied cooperation and effectively sealed the strategic fate of Nazi Germany.
